BasketEntry.description:
v3 E3: buy every open sibling of an event as one all-or-nothing basket when the set
identity leaves an edge. YES set: Σ P(yes) ≤ 1 − c; NO set: Σ P(no) ≤ (N − 1) − c, with
c = Σ leg fees + one tick per leg + `min_edge`.

Order.description:
v3 E1: how signals become orders. LIMIT is the default for all research: a buy limit is
the signal price plus `limit_offset_ticks`, a sell limit is the signal price minus it, and
the order rests for `ttl_bars` bars before it expires. MARKET keeps v2 behaviour and is
flagged as having no price protection.
Order.title: Order

PrintTrigger.description:
v3 E4 / S3: enter when a taker print of at least `min_notional` by one of `wallets` (any
wallet when null) lands in the bar. The signal remembers the wallet, so a WALLET_SELL exit
can watch for its sale.
PrintTrigger.title: PrintTrigger

Side.description:
§3.3 — there is no shorting; short YES is expressed as BUY_NO. EITHER makes both tokens of
each market candidates, so the entry rules choose the side (a price ≥ 0.9 rule buys the
favourite, whichever outcome that is); a market never holds both sides at once.
Side.title: Side

min_order_policy.description: When the sized order is below the market's minimum order size: SKIP rejects it (REJECTED_MIN_SIZE); ROUND_UP places the minimum instead, if cash, exposure headroom, max_notional_per_trade and the liquidity cap all still allow it and it is at most round_up_max_multiple times the requested notional.
min_order_policy.title: Min Order Policy

deadline_types.description: v3 S2: keep only markets whose question has this deadline type (BY: 'by/before <date>', ON: 'on/at <date>' or a fixture, NONE: neither). Parsed from the question text, known at listing.
